Elliptic curves

Source: R/ntheory.R
EllipticCurve.Rd

EllipticCurve(a4, a6, a1, a2, a3, modulus) is the curve y^2 + a1*x*y + a3*y = x^3 + a2*x^2 + a4*x + a6 over the rationals (modulus = 0) or over the integers modulo a prime. The result holds the fields characteristic, discriminant, is_singular and j_invariant, and the methods point(x, y, z = 1) (also EllipticCurvePoint()), point_at_infinity(), points() (a matrix of the affine points over a finite field), points_x(x), torsion_points(), minimal(), order() and rank(). Points support +, -, * by an integer and ==, and point_order() gives the order of a point (Inf for infinite order).

Usage

EllipticCurve(a4, a6, a1 = 0, a2 = 0, a3 = 0, modulus = 0)

EllipticCurvePoint(x, y, z, curve)

point_order(p)

Arguments

a4, a6, a1, a2, a3

Coefficients.

modulus

0, or a prime.

x, y, z

Projective coordinates.

curve

An EllipticCurve.

p

A point.

Value

An EllipticCurve environment, or an EllipticCurvePoint.

Details

Several SymPy defects are fixed: order() counts the point at infinity, so it is the order of the group; a point P with P == -P has order 2 even when a1 or a3 is nonzero; point_order() over the rationals relies on Mazur's bound of 12 rather than integral coordinates; torsion_points() works through an integral short model, so it also finds the torsion of curves with rational coefficients; and the discriminant of a curve with rational coefficients is exact rather than truncated. Over a finite field, points() lists the affine points as a numeric matrix, so the modulus must be below 2^53, and points_x(x) returns a list of list(x, y).

Examples

e <- EllipticCurve(-1, 9)
p <- e$point(0, 3)
q <- e$point(-1, 3)
p + q
#> (1, -3) 
2 * p + q
#> (35, 207) 
e$discriminant
#> [1] -34928
EllipticCurve(0, 1)$torsion_points()
#> [[1]]
#> O 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> (-1, 0) 
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> (0, 1) 
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> (0, -1) 
#> 
#> [[5]]
#> (2, 3) 
#> 
#> [[6]]
#> (2, -3) 
#> 
f <- EllipticCurve(1, 0, modulus = 19)
f$order()
#> [1] 20
point_order(f$point(3, 7))
#> [1] 20
